main_body: A dark column shaft (rows 15-40) with three gold ring ornaments, capped top and bottom by grey stone blocks (rows 8-14 and 40-47). It reads as a flat front view of a capped pillar.
top_band: Grey cap, rows 9-12, roughly L=115-138 with a 1-row highlight at row 12. At x=8 the cap is mid-grey (L=115) over rows 9-11, then a highlight, then a dark underside at rows 13-14. It is no wider than the shaft by much and is a straight rectangular band, not an ellipse.
evidence: Rule 12 for columns: the top must be a visible top face, an ellipse or a plate wider than the shaft, at least 4 rows tall and clearly lighter than the shaft. Here the cap is a straight rectangular block of about 3 light rows (9-11, L=115) with a highlight row 12. It sits over a dark underside (rows 13-16) and is barely wider than the body. This matches the red 'flat band cap' in the guide. The scan shows the cap tone (L=115) is the same as the lighter shaft edge at x=5, so it reads as the front of a stone block and not as a top surface. The gold ring details are painted flat on a dark front with no inset. No top surface is clearly visible, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. The dark edge pixels are 100% neutral (#19171c), so the outline is the near-black sticker look and not a tint of the adjacent material. The shaft is a nearly flat dark fill with three small gold rings, and the caps are 2-3 grey tones with no grain, speckle or per-block shading. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0% only because the piece is narrow. Overall it is much shallower and flatter than the reference stall and well.
